title: The universal form
hookLine: Arjuna gets what he asked for, and it's brighter than a thousand suns
carry: the whole universe lives in one god
last: DIVYAM CHAKSHUH — DARSHAN: THE SIGHT OF GOD IS A GIFT.

cards: One sun at noon is already too bright to look at. Add a second beside it. Then ten.
Then a hundred. Then a thousand, all at once, all blazing. You can't look at it.

You can't look away. That's the measure the Gita reaches for when Arjuna, with his new divine eye, finally sees what he asked to see. Sanjaya, telling it, has no ordinary comparison left, so he stacks up suns.

teach.b: Sanjaya tells it. Having spoken, the great lord of yoga showed Arjuna his supreme form. Many mouths and eyes, many wonders, divine ornaments, divine weapons raised.

teach.h: THE LIGHT OF A THOUSAND SUNS.
teach.b: Verse twelve: if the light of a thousand suns were to blaze up in the sky all at once, it might be like the splendor of that great being.
Verse thirteen: there, in the body of the god of gods, Arjuna saw the whole universe, divided in countless ways, gathered as one. He bows his head, joins his palms, and speaks. At first it's wonder.
I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of beings. Brahma on his lotus, the sages, the divine serpents. I see you everywhere, with countless arms and eyes.

teach.h: NO END, NO MIDDLE, NO BEGINNING.
teach.b: No end, no middle, no beginning. The sun and moon are your eyes. Then it turns.
The mouths have fangs. The worlds are trembling, and so am I.

Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies, the men he's about to fight, his own teachers and great-uncle among them, rushing into those mouths like rivers running into the ocean, like moths flying into a flame.
It's beautiful and it's terrifying, and the Gita doesn't soften either. Verse thirty-one: tell me, who are you, in this fierce form? I bow to you.

Be gracious. I want to understand you; I don't know what you're doing. That's the vishvarupa, the universal form, and it carries one of Hinduism's biggest teachings: God isn't one being among many, off somewhere.
Every god, every star, every life and every ending is held inside one God. It's why so many Hindus bow to the divine in everything, including the parts that frighten us.

how: The vishvarupa, the universal form of Gita chapter eleven, is painted, sculpted and staged across Hindu art and temple traditions, and many devotees read the chapter with awe as the Gita's great vision.

o: the beauty of nature seen as divine
the whole universe seen at once in God's body
a god who can take on any shape he likes

games.q: what's inside the vision — tap the pairs.
p: the light of a thousand suns

s: the vision is only beautiful and calm
it turns terrifying: fangs, trembling worlds, warriors rushing into the mouths.
in the vision, the warriors rush into the mouths like rivers into the sea
verse 28: like rivers running to the ocean; verse 29: like moths into a flame.
Arjuna understands the vision right away
verse 31: who are you, in this fierce form? I don't know what you're doing.

games.q: you're Arjuna. you asked to see God's true form, and it's more terrible than you imagined. what do you do?
o: close your eyes and refuse to look.
bow, and ask: who are you, in this fierce form?
games.why: he bows and asks, verse 31: tell me who you are. be gracious. the answer comes tomorrow.

practice: Feel your own body breathing, then widen: the room, the street, the city, the whole country at this hour, people waking and sleeping, being born and dying, then the earth turning in sunlight.
Let it be too big to hold, and notice what that feels like: wonder, fear, or both. Then, if you pray, end as Arjuna did, palms joined, with a small bow; if not, simply come back to one breath.

wordCard.voice: Vishvarupa. The universal form: the whole universe seen at once in God's body, brighter than a thousand suns, wonderful and terrible.

orig.note: Sanskrit: vishvarupa, the universal form; vishva (all, the universe) + rupa (form).

carryVoice: Your line: the whole universe lives in one God. Arjuna asked to see, and he saw. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 11.9–11.14 (the form revealed; a thousand suns)
Bhagavad Gita 11.15–11.31 (Arjuna's description; who are you?)
